why: Each transaction links its user to its device and its card, so a fraud ring is a connected component of the user-device-card graph. Union all three keys per row, then count distinct users sharing the target's root.
hints: Users are linked transitively through shared devices or cards. What structure answers 'which users end up in the same group'?
Union-find over tagged keys (user, device, card). Each transaction unions its user with its device and its card.
After processing all rows, count users whose root equals the target's root. O(T alpha(T)). BFS over a bipartite user-identifier graph also works.
pitfalls: Tag keys by type so device 'X1' and card 'X1' are not merged by accident.
A user with no shared identifiers still forms a ring of size 1.
